quest.title: Echoes of an Unfinished Past
quest.description: You run into Vernadska, the self-proclaimed priestess, again on Hiisi Island. This time, she's trying to get into a sanctum...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x450, Primogem x50, Mora x50000, Hero's Wit x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x4

dialogues.text: #Oh! It's {NICKNAME} and Paimon! Nice to see you again!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um... Miss Priestess, have we met somewhere before? You don't seem that familiar to Paimon...
Hey! It's me! Seriously, we met not long ago... Can't you recognize me by my voice?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh yeah, it's you! You're the one from back when— Uhh... Wait, who are you exactly? This is starting to sound like some kinda weird scam...

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: Aww, my adorable little Paimon didn't even recognize me... That really stings. But I'll let it slide — after all, you did call me "Miss Priestess." I guess it's fair, since I never took off my helmet back at Thunderclap Reef...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, hang on! Don't tell Paimon... you're Verna!? You're really, actually a priestess from the Frostmoon Scions!?

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: E—Excuse you! That's a weird way to say hello! Seriously, you won't find a priestess more reliable than me anywhere else! There was never any reason to doubt me in the first place!

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: Ahem! Anyway, this must be the Moon Mai{RUBY#[D]Kuutar}den's guidance at work — how else could I be so fortunate as to run into you both at a time like this?

choices.text: Well, we were just passing through...

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Exactly! That's what we call fate. "With her silver spindle, she weaves paths as one, whether they be of the rich, or the—" Uh, or the...

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: #Anyway, let's forget about all that. {NICKNAME}, Paimon, you remember what that imposter said before, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You mean that priestess-looking lady who seemed more legit than you? She said she'd be waiting at the Court of the First Edict... or something like that?

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Ahem... That "more legit than you" bit was totally uncalled for. But since you've got such a good memory, Paimon, and since you're both going to help me out later, I'll let it slide!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! Paimon hasn't agreed to help you out yet! Why is it that every time we talk to you, we end up second-guessing reality...?

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Uh, don't sweat the details! More importantly, I've already come up with a flawless, super-ultra reliable plan. We'll catch that imposter in no time!

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Think about it. She said she'd be waiting in the sealed-off sanctum no one can even get into, right? So obviously...

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: She wants us to get curious and break the seal, letting her sneak in and snatch whatever treasure's inside!

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: And my super-foolproof plan is to turn the tables on her! Once we open the gates of the sanctum, she'll definitely show up, and that's when we'll catch her!

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Pretty solid plan, right? I'd say it'd hold up just fine against those top-notch detectives from Papa Wrench's books!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Seriously?! That sounds even crazier than the plan you had at Thunderclap Reef! You just told us no one's been able to unseal the Court of the First Edict for centuries!

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Only because they didn't have me, along with the super reliable tag-team combination that is the two of you!

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: After we parted ways, I've been thinking... Since the Court of the First Edict was sealed by kuuvahki, maybe we can disrupt it the same way we did at Thunderclap Reef...

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: And so— Ta-dah! See? I had my little Krakas look for more of those special fragments, and I pieced them all together!

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: And the moment I managed to distract Eveliina, bam! You two showed up! Tell me we're not fated to reunite!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Fated? More like fatal! Are you sure this won't mess up the weather on Hiisi Island like it did back at Thunderclap Reef?

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: No worries! This time, I'll be in full control of the kuuvahki. And besides, everything turned out just fine back at the Reef, didn't it?

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: #Now then! {NICKNAME}, Paimon, prepare to witness the miracle of science!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: W—Wait! If someone's gotta throw it, let us do it! If we leave it to you, this already sketchy plan's bound to get even sketchier...

choices.text: I have a bad feeling about this...

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Now now, bad feelings have no place in the Moon Goddess's guidance! Since we're all here, this must surely be a good omen... no, a great omen!

talks.objective: Throw fragment(s) to open the sealed sanctum

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: Hehe, just like I predicted! See? As long as we follow the guidance of the Moon Goddess, everything'll fall right into place!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, if you say so... But are we really sure it's a good idea to open up a place that's been sealed for centuries?

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: Oh, it'll be totally fine! You've got the most trustworthy priestess of the Frostmoon Scions right here, there's absolutely nothing to worry abou—

dialogues.speaker: Ehrnrooth
dialogues.text: Krodo! Did you see where those suspicious intruders were headed?

dialogues.speaker: Krodo
dialogues.text: They took off toward the Court of the First Edict. Not many places to hide around here, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Rahetar
dialogues.text: Hmph. You two, check on the seal. I'll inform the Lady Moonchanter. Let's see them try getting away...

dialogues.speaker: Rahetar
dialogues.text: Causing trouble in the sacred lands of the Frost Moon... They've got a death wish! The only way they're getting out of this in one piece is if they're somehow the Lady Kuu{RUBY#[D]Moon Maiden}tar herself...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhh... Verna? Still wanna tell us "there's absolutely nothing to worry about"?

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: I... Uhh... Ahaha! Yep! That's right! There's absolutely nothing to worry about! Now that the seal's been opened, all we have to do is set a trap and wait for that imposter to walk right into our hands...

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: #...I'm sorry, I'm so sorry! There's absolutely everything to worry about! I should never have messed with the seal... What do we do now?! Help me, {NICKNAME}, please! *sobs*...

choices.text: Yelling for help like a crybaby doesn't mean someone's magically going to save your butt!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Exactly! Well, since the seal's already broken, we might as well head in and take a look... But Verna, you'd better remember to say sorry to everyone in the Frostmoon Scions when we're done here!

choices.text: No turning back now. Let's see what's inside.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, since the seal's already broken, we might as well head in and take a look... But Verna, you'd better make sure to say sorry to everyone you dragged into this!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Umm... Verna, where are we? This doesn't really look like a sanctum...

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: Yeah, it really doesn't... Ahem! I mean, that's not important! Don't worry! This place has things that resemble Moonlanes, so that means the Moon Maiden is still guiding us... p—probably!

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: Let us follow the path illuminated by the moonlight, and leave the rest to the will of the moon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That actually sounded pretty priestess-y coming from you, Verna... Wait, no! Isn't that just a fancy way of saying "I don't know what to do, let's just leave it to fate"?!

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: Hey! What do you mean "pretty priestess-y"? Have you ever met a priestess who's anything less than super priestess-y?

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: You've gotta have as much faith in the Moon Maiden's guidance as you do in the power of science! Besides, it's not like we've found any other way down...

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: Come on, I told you there's nothing to worry about! See? This is the power of science!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Hurray! The power of scien— Hey, wait a second! You almost had Paimon fooled! This has nothing to do with science! It was just {NICKNAME} tossing the fragments up there!

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: #Well, since the super reliable {NICKNAME} is also someone who believes in science, I guess that explanation works too.

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: Alright! "Since the Moon Ma{RUBY#[D]Kuutar}iden has spun a silvery path for us, what awaits beyond the threshold must be..." Umm... wait, how did the rest of it go again...?

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: Ahem, anyway... since the Moonlane has appeared, it means our plan is working fine. All we need to do is follow it. This is the guidance of the Moon Goddess... Yep!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A—Are you sure? Paimon thinks there's a good chance this path doesn't lead to our destination, but rather somewhere higher up...

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: Come on, Paimon, come on! You've got a super reliable priestess and a super reliable adventurer on your side — what's there to worry about?

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: We'd better get moving, before the other priestesses show up— Ahem, I mean, while the Moon Goddess is still showing us the way! Onward and upward!

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: Hmm? It's awfully quiet... Ehrnrooth and Uncle Krodo aren't here either. Weren't they hot on our trail?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Maybe all the noise we made earlier got their attention, and they ran off to check somewhere else?

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: #Aha, I get it now! This must be Lady Aila's divine guidance. Even my luck's looking up now that I'm with someone as reliable as you, {NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, okay, save the celebration for later! You do remember you still owe everybody else an apology for the trouble you caused, right?

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: Apology? ... Ahem, r—right, yes, of course I do! I'm not the type to get so caught up in reading Lady Aila's records that I forget everything else!

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: I swear by my mortal name in this sublunary sphere that I'll give everybody a proper and heartfelt apology! It's just... Uh, I'll need to think carefully about how to phrase it first...

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: Oh! And while we were at work earlier, I came up with a super scientific plan!

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: Since I have to apologize anyway, why don't we finish checking out the sanctum first before looking for Lady Lauma? That way, we can save time and make my eventual apology more efficient!

dialogues.speaker: Rahetar
dialogues.text: A sound plan, I should say.

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: See? The power of science is— wait, huh!? Aunt Rahetar? When did you get here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Waaah, you scared us! Umm... We didn't mean to sneak into the Court of the First Edict! It's just... Verna said...

dialogues.speaker: Rahetar
dialogues.text: No need to explain. This place may be sealed, but it is not forbidden territory. If outsiders like you were able to enter, then perhaps it was the will of the moonlight.

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: Exactly! This is all part of the Moon M{RUBY#[D]Kuutar}aiden's sacred guidance! Just like the poems say—

dialogues.speaker: Rahetar
dialogues.text: As for you, Vernadska, you're coming with me. The Lady Moonchanter wants to see you — in person.

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: Huh!? Wait, no, Aunt Rahetar, didn't you just say—

dialogues.speaker: Rahetar
dialogues.text: As a priestess, you acted without permission, broke the rules, and tampered with taboos. Aside from outright murder, you've flouted every major law we have.

dialogues.speaker: Rahetar
dialogues.text: Now come. Or would you rather the Lady Moonchanter come fetch you herself?

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: #Uhh... {NICKNAME}, Paimon! I'll explain everything later! I swear! But first, I—I'll need—

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Before Verna can finish her sentence, Rahetar drags her off...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well... She sure dug that grave nice and deep for herself, didn't she?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Still, we've got no idea what this Lady Aila wanted us to do. But this sword she left behind...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... If it was meant for us, we might as well hang onto it for now. Looks like a real Frostmoon relic, anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, something about this place feels off compared to what Paimon imagined a sanctum would be... It doesn't feel all that sacred. Smells kinda funny instead...

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: Haha, well, it has been sealed for 500 years, y'know? Scientifically speaking, rusted metal giving off a blood-like smell isn't too surprising.

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: By the way, the hymns say that before Lady Aila sealed it, this was where all the Frostmoon followers held their ceremonies! So it's super sacred, really!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Calling it "super sacred" just makes it sound less sacred by the minute!

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: Oh, come on, don't get hung up on the wording! Look over there — that's the Verdant Crest! Legend says it's the sacred tree that witnessed the birth of the Moon Mai{RUBY#[D]Kuutar}den!

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: And that pool over there... Uh, if I'm guessing right, that should be the ever-flowing White S{RUBY#[D]Vellamo}pring, blessed by Lady Aila herself!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do you really have to guess? Also, are you sure you didn't just make those names up?

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: Hey! I might be a fairly reliable priestess, but even I've never seen these sacred relics from five hundred years ago with my own eyes!

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: #Nor did I ever think I'd get to see something this historically significant... I'm so lucky. All thanks to you, {NICKNAME} and Paimon!

choices.text: Let's stay here for a bit.

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: #Yes, yes, no problem! I'll do whatever you say, {NICKNAME}!

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Just standing in place does feel like a waste, though... Since we're here, why not take a quick walk around?

choices.text: Just remember to apologize to everyone after we get out.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm? There's something beneath the water. Is that a sword?

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: Huh? Why would there be a sword here? ...Wait. Hold on. Could this be the ritual sword forged from Hyperborean moonlight that Lady Aila supposedly left behind...!?

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: The blade that was used to offer up the very first drop of blood under the new moon... Whoa!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: I—It's a kuuhenki... Hmm, does it want us to follow it?

dialogues.speaker: Aila
dialogues.text: Ah, you're here. Wait, that will get the altar dirty...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eek! When the heck did you get in here? We were the ones who opened the seal first... right?

choices.text: Something's off...

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: You're right... But this isn't just "off." It looks like this is a residual image left behind by the Moon Goddes{RUBY#[D]kuuvahki}s's blessing...

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: And it's been left inside the Court of the First Edict... Maybe this... might be the first Moonchanter herself, Lady Aila...

choices.text: Is that really possible?

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: S—Scientifically speaking, it's impossible — but if this is truly Lady Aila, then it wouldn't be surprising for her power to be unscientifically potent...

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Oh my days... I can't believe I kept calling THE Lady Aila an imposter... Thank the Moon Goddess she can't hear me anymore...

choices.text: And that explains why her words were always so hard to understand...

response.speaker: Aila
response.text: There, that should do it.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (This power... is the Lady Aila before us really just a lingering image?)

response.speaker: Unknown Voice
response.text: ...What did you do, Miss Aila?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Aaahh! W—Where did that voice just come from?!

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Hmm... Maybe it got recorded along with the first Moonchanter's image? I mean, even the Moon Goddes{RUBY#[D]kuuvahki}s's blessing couldn't be precise enough to capture just one person's voice, right?

response.speaker: Aila
response.text: Hehe... There's no need to be so tense. That woman who shares my bloodline surely showed you a few of these low-brow tricks before, hmm?

response.speaker: Aila
response.text: This is merely a blessing that records awareness, so that <color=#00E1FFFF>the brave warrior over there</color> can hear our words.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: P—Paimon's not dreaming, is she? Paimon swears she just looked right at us!

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Come on, Paimon, you're most definitely dreaming. What we're seeing now was recorded five hundred years ago, there's no way she could actually see us...

response.speaker: Unknown Voice
response.text: "Over there"? But I don't see anyone...

response.speaker: Unknown Voice
response.text: Ah, never mind. I probably wouldn't understand even if you explained it to me. And whatever tangled past lies between you and her... I'm in no position to judge. Regardless, thank you for your help, Miss Aila.

response.speaker: Unknown Voice
response.text: Lovia should have known better. The wounds left in the wake of the atrocities that old witch inflicted upon you both run deep — of course, the scars fester with resentment. What surprises me is that she trusted you so deeply.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, Verna, who's this Lovia they mentioned? Paimon feels like she's heard that name before...

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: She was the leader of Frostmoon Scions five hundred years ago, but she was stricken from memory for the sin of blasphemy. Normally, only senior — and super reliable — priestesses like me would even know about her...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, if even someone like you knows about her, then it can't be that much of a secret, can it...?

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Hey! Rude! What do you mean, "someone like me"? But seriously, her identity should be top secret. Ordinary followers and folks from the outside aren't supposed to have even heard that name.

response.speaker: Aila
response.text: Resentment? For what? Everything you and I went through was always meant to be. There is no past or future — because the past is the future.

response.speaker: Aila
response.text: Your gaze is upon me now, but all you can see is this one fleeting moment. Thanks to Lovia's blessing — the blessing of our ancestors — I can see every moment.

response.speaker: Aila
response.text: Your arrival... Lovia's end... all threads of a tapestry too vast for me to tell. And yet — how it thrills me.

response.speaker: Aila
response.text: She trusted me because I heeded her every word. And when the Lady of the{RUBY#[D]Tuonetar} Underworld guided my hand to sever her thread... Even then, she should have rejoiced.

response.speaker: Aila
response.text: As for you... You'll be leaving this place soon, won't you, Mr. Solovei?

response.speaker: Unknown Voice
response.text: My role here is finished. The believers outside already hail you as their new prophet... and at last, you no longer need to endure the suffering imposed on you.

response.speaker: Unknown Voice
response.text: I still have things I must do. I need to uncover that mad monk's true intentions. For my fallen friend and the people of this land, he must pay for what he has done.

response.speaker: Unknown Voice
response.text: With Lovia's years of secret correspondence with him as evidence, tracing his steps should be much easier. Once again, thank you for your help, Miss Aila.

response.speaker: Aila
response.text: Ah, so you still don't know a thing... but that's alright. You will soon enough.

response.speaker: Unknown Voice
response.text: I'll take that as an encouragement.

response.speaker: Aila
response.text: To me, it's already happened. Twice shall that serpent fall — first strangled by the flesh of the faithless, then shrinking away before the light you and I ignite together.

response.speaker: Aila
response.text: But you shan't be the one to cut off its thread, because that fate does not belong to you.

response.speaker: Unknown Voice
response.text: I don't believe in fate. I'll just do what I can.

response.speaker: Aila
response.text: Then do what you can. Before the lanterns are lit, I will be here waiting — for you are the hero meant to protect "Elysium."

response.speaker: Aila
response.text: And you... Forgive me for drawing you here this way. Your thread simply would not catch in the loom of this sublunary sphere, so I had to guide you with those stones. Fitting, for they are just as out of place in this world as you are.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh... Huh!? Verna, what's going on? Are you still sure she isn't talking to us!?

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: W—Well, not anymore! Those stones we saw earlier only fell recently... how could Lady Aila have known about them five hundred years ago...?

response.speaker: Aila
response.text: By way of apology, I left the last sword forged by the apostle of the golden city using moonlight in the ever-flowing White Spring. After centuries, any bloodstains on its blade should have been washed away.

response.speaker: Aila
response.text: Please accept this humble gift. Though your fate remains unclear to me, I choose to believe you are the hero of this sublunary sphere — the one destined to fell the undying serpent on our behalf.

response.speaker: Aila
response.text: This will probably be the last time we meet. If you follow the light and find those who share my bloodline, then you will come to understand my words.

response.speaker: Unknown Voice
response.text: ...Are you... talking to someone?

response.speaker: Aila
response.text: It's nothing. Now, please don't let me keep you any longer, Mr. Solovei. I must begin sealing this place at once.

response.speaker: Aila
response.text: I hold no resentment toward Lovia. But our children must not be stained by her sins.

response.speaker: Aila
response.text: That's why the evil and corruption she wrought must be buried... I will seal them all here. This, too, is a part of our preparation for the birth of a god.

response.speaker: Aila
response.text: We are all tainted by sin... How could we ever hope to behold the moonlight in its purest form?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: She vanished...

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: #So... just like back at Thunderclap Reef, it was Lady Aila who guided us to break the sanctum's seal, all so you could retrieve the sword she left behind, {NICKNAME}...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Come to think of it, Miss Alia said something similar to us back at the Pillar of Embla...

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Oh, I see, I see— wait a moment. I don't recognize that name. Who is this Alia?

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You briefly explained to Verna about the battle alongside the Ratniki...\n"Twice shall that undying serpent rise again, but thrice shall he be struck down..."\n"And at last shall he be laid to rest by the heroes of the sublunary sphere..."

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Wow... I'm still not totally sure what just happened, but you've taken down that undying serpent either way, yes?

choices.text: That's right, I am the hero foretold in the prophecy!

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Heh, I know, right? I knew that even back at Thunderclap Reef! You don't need a prophecy to prove it — you've always been someone I could count on!

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: But... who is this Alia, anyway? She says she's from five hundred years ago, but I've never seen that name in any records from back then...

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Well, whatever! Since Lady Aila brought it up, let's go find that sword!

choices.text: Ahem... It was a team effort.
And that explains why she seemed like a more legit priestess than you...

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: W—Well, of course! I may be reliable, but I'm still just a regular priestess. There's no way I could compare to the great Lady Aila, who witnessed the birth of the Moon Ma{RUBY#[D]Kuutar}iden!

choices.text: Doesn't sound very... Umm... scientific.
Good thing the treasure chests are still here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, you're right... Wait, now's not the time for that! So... just who are you, Miss Priestess-y-Looking Priestess?

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: If I may, I suspect she's more of a "what" than a "who" by now...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eek! Don't say creepy stuff like that all of a sudden! Are you saying she's a...

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: No, no! That's not what I meant! There's no such thing as ghosts... At least, I think so...? But she seems more like a lingering image left behind by the Moon Goddes{RUBY#[D]kuuvahki}s's blessing...

talks.objective: Enter the Court of the First Edict

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: Hmm? It's awfully quiet... Ehrnrooth and Uncle Krodo aren't here either. Weren't they hot on our trail?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Maybe all the noise we made earlier got their attention, and they ran off to check somewhere else?

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: #Aha, I get it now! This must be Lady Aila's divine guidance. Even my luck's looking up now that I'm with someone as reliable as you, {NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, okay, save the celebration for later! You do remember you still owe everybody else an apology for the trouble you caused, right?

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: Apology? ... Ahem, r—right, yes, of course I do! I'm not the type to get so caught up in reading Lady Aila's records that I forget everything else!

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: I swear by my mortal name in this sublunary sphere that I'll give everybody a proper and heartfelt apology! It's just... Uh, I'll need to think carefully about how to phrase it first...

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: Oh! And while we were at work earlier, I came up with a super scientific plan!

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: Since I have to apologize anyway, why don't we finish checking out the sanctum first before looking for Lady Lauma? That way, we can save time and make my eventual apology more efficient!

dialogues.speaker: Rahetar
dialogues.text: A sound plan, I should say.

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: See? The power of science is— wait, huh!? Aunt Rahetar? When did you get here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Waaah, you scared us! Umm... We didn't mean to sneak into the Court of the First Edict! It's just... Verna said...

dialogues.speaker: Rahetar
dialogues.text: No need to explain. This place may be sealed, but it is not forbidden territory. If outsiders like you were able to enter, then perhaps it was the will of the moonlight.

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: Exactly! This is all part of the Moon M{RUBY#[D]Kuutar}aiden's sacred guidance! Look, Aunt Rahetar, we even found something Lady Aila left for—

dialogues.speaker: Rahetar
dialogues.text: As for you, Vernadska, you're coming with me. The Lady Moonchanter wants to see you — in person.

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: Huh!? Wait, no, Aunt Rahetar, didn't you just say—

dialogues.speaker: Rahetar
dialogues.text: As a priestess, you acted without permission, broke the rules, and tampered with taboos. Aside from outright murder, you've flouted every major law we have.

dialogues.speaker: Rahetar
dialogues.text: Now come. Or would you rather the Lady Moonchanter come fetch you herself?

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: #Uhh... {NICKNAME}, Paimon! I'll explain everything later! I swear! But first, I—I'll need—

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Before Verna can finish her sentence, Rahetar drags her off...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well... She sure dug that grave nice and deep for herself, didn't she?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But since we've already taken down the undying serpent, I suppose that means we've fulfilled the task the first Moonchanter entrusted to us, right?

talks.objective: Enter the Court of the First Edict
Investigate the Court of the First Edict
Investigate the Court of the First Edict
Investigate the Court of the First Edict

dialogues.speaker: Aila
dialogues.text: Ah, you're here. Wait, that will get the altar dirty...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eek! When the heck did you get in here? We were the ones who opened the seal first... right?

choices.text: Something's off...

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: You're right... But this isn't just "off." It looks like this is a residual image left behind by the Moon Goddes{RUBY#[D]kuuvahki}s's blessing...

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: And it's been left inside the Court of the First Edict... Maybe this... might be the first Moonchanter herself, Lady Aila...

choices.text: Is that really possible?

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: S—Scientifically speaking, it's impossible — but if this is truly Lady Aila, then it wouldn't be surprising for her power to be unscientifically potent...

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Oh my days... I can't believe I kept calling THE Lady Aila an imposter... Thank the Moon Goddess she can't hear me anymore...

choices.text: And that explains why her words were always so hard to understand...

response.speaker: Aila
response.text: There, that should do it.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (This power... is the Lady Aila before us really just a lingering image?)

response.speaker: Unknown Voice
response.text: ...What did you do, Miss Aila?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Aaahh! W—Where did that voice just come from?!

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Hmm... Maybe it got recorded along with the first Moonchanter's image? I mean, even the Moon Goddes{RUBY#[D]kuuvahki}s's blessing couldn't be precise enough to capture just one person's voice, right?

response.speaker: Aila
response.text: Hehe... There's no need to be so tense. That woman who shares my bloodline surely showed you a few of these low-brow tricks before, hmm?

response.speaker: Aila
response.text: This is merely a blessing that records awareness, so that <color=#00E1FFFF>the brave warrior over there</color> can hear our words.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: P—Paimon's not dreaming, is she? Paimon swears she just looked right at us!

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Come on, Paimon, you're most definitely dreaming. What we're seeing now was recorded five hundred years ago, there's no way she could actually see us...

response.speaker: Unknown Voice
response.text: "Over there"? But I don't see anyone...

response.speaker: Unknown Voice
response.text: Ah, never mind. I probably wouldn't understand even if you explained it to me. And whatever tangled past lies between you and her... I'm in no position to judge. Regardless, thank you for your help, Miss Aila.

response.speaker: Unknown Voice
response.text: Lovia should have known better. The wounds left in the wake of the atrocities that old witch inflicted upon you both run deep — of course, the scars fester with resentment. What surprises me is that she trusted you so deeply.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, Verna, who's this Lovia they mentioned? Paimon feels like she's heard that name before...

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: She was the leader of Frostmoon Scions five hundred years ago, but she was stricken from memory for the sin of blasphemy. Normally, only senior — and super reliable — priestesses like me would even know about her...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, if even someone like you knows about her, then it can't be that much of a secret, can it...?

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Hey! Rude! What do you mean, "someone like me"? But seriously, her identity should be top secret. Ordinary followers and folks from the outside aren't supposed to have even heard that name.

response.speaker: Aila
response.text: Resentment? For what? Everything you and I went through was always meant to be. There is no past or future — because the past is the future.

response.speaker: Aila
response.text: Your gaze is upon me now, but all you can see is this one fleeting moment. Thanks to Lovia's blessing — the blessing of our ancestors — I can see every moment.

response.speaker: Aila
response.text: Your arrival... Lovia's end... all threads of a tapestry too vast for me to tell. And yet — how it thrills me.

response.speaker: Aila
response.text: She trusted me because I heeded her every word. And when the Lady of the{RUBY#[D]Tuonetar} Underworld guided my hand to sever her thread... Even then, she should have rejoiced.

response.speaker: Aila
response.text: As for you... You'll be leaving this place soon, won't you, Mr. Solovei?

response.speaker: Unknown Voice
response.text: My role here is finished. The believers outside already hail you as their new prophet... and at last, you no longer need to endure the suffering imposed on you.

response.speaker: Unknown Voice
response.text: I still have things I must do. I need to uncover that mad monk's true intentions. For my fallen friend and the people of this land, he must pay for what he has done.

response.speaker: Unknown Voice
response.text: With Lovia's years of secret correspondence with him as evidence, tracing his steps should be much easier. Once again, thank you for your help, Miss Aila.

response.speaker: Aila
response.text: Ah, so you still don't know a thing... but that's alright. You will soon enough.

response.speaker: Unknown Voice
response.text: I'll take that as an encouragement.

response.speaker: Aila
response.text: To me, it's already happened. Twice shall that serpent fall — first strangled by the flesh of the faithless, then shrinking away before the light you and I ignite together.

response.speaker: Aila
response.text: But you shan't be the one to cut off its thread, because that fate does not belong to you.

response.speaker: Unknown Voice
response.text: I don't believe in fate. I'll just do what I can.

response.speaker: Aila
response.text: Then do what you can. Before the lanterns are lit, I will be here waiting — for you are the hero meant to protect "Elysium."

response.speaker: Aila
response.text: And you... Forgive me for drawing you here this way. Your thread simply would not catch in the loom of this sublunary sphere, so I had to guide you with those stones. Fitting, for they are just as out of place in this world as you are.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh... Huh!? Verna, what's going on? Are you still sure she isn't talking to us!?

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: W—Well, not anymore! Those stones we saw earlier only fell recently... how could Lady Aila have known about them five hundred years ago...?

response.speaker: Aila
response.text: By way of apology, I left the last sword forged by the apostle of the golden city using moonlight in the ever-flowing White Spring. After centuries, any bloodstains on its blade should have been washed away.

response.speaker: Aila
response.text: Please accept this humble gift. Though your fate remains unclear to me, I choose to believe you are the hero of this sublunary sphere — the one destined to fell the undying serpent on our behalf.

response.speaker: Aila
response.text: This will probably be the last time we meet. If you follow the light and find those who share my bloodline, then you will come to understand my words.

response.speaker: Unknown Voice
response.text: ...Are you... talking to someone?

response.speaker: Aila
response.text: It's nothing. Now, please don't let me keep you any longer, Mr. Solovei. I must begin sealing this place at once.

response.speaker: Aila
response.text: I hold no resentment toward Lovia. But our children must not be stained by her sins.

response.speaker: Aila
response.text: That's why the evil and corruption she wrought must be buried... I will seal them all here. This, too, is a part of our preparation for the birth of a god.

response.speaker: Aila
response.text: We are all tainted by sin... How could we ever hope to behold the moonlight in its purest form?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: She vanished...

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: #So... just like back at Thunderclap Reef, it was Lady Aila who guided us to break the sanctum's seal, all so you could retrieve the sword she left behind, {NICKNAME}...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But Paimon still doesn't get it. Why would Aila give us her sword? And what's this "undying serpent" stuff all about? We're not gonna have to fight some giant snake next, are we?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Anyway, {NICKNAME}, let's retrieve that sword first!

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: R—Right! If someone as reliable as Lady Aila said it, there must be a reason. Maybe it'll all start to click once we get that sword!

choices.text: And that explains why she seemed like a more legit priestess than you...

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: W—Well, of course! I may be reliable, but I'm still just a regular priestess. There's no way I could compare to the great Lady Aila who witnessed the birth of the Moon Ma{RUBY#[D]Kuutar}iden!

choices.text: Doesn't sound very... Umm... scientific.
Good thing the treasure chests are still here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, you're right... Wait, now's not the time for that! So... just who are you, Miss Priestess-y-Looking Priestess?

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: If I may, I suspect she's more of a "what" than a "who" by now...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eek! Don't say creepy stuff like that all of a sudden! Are you saying she's a...

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: No, no! That's not what I meant! There's no such thing as ghosts... At least, I think so...? But she seems more like a lingering image left behind by the Moon Goddes{RUBY#[D]kuuvahki}s's blessing...

talks.objective: Investigate the sword Aila left behind

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Hmm... this must be the sword Aila was talking about, right? How about it, {NICKNAME}? Did you figure anything out?

choices.text: Not a thing.

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Ugh, looks like we really will have to investigate this whole place, huh? But if we hang around too long, Ehrnrooth, Uncle Krodo, and the others might find the entrance too...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Actually, with all the noise we made just now, there's probably no one on this whole island who hasn't been drawn this way...

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Ugh, fine, guess we've got no choice... We've got the sword now, and Lady Aila didn't exactly tell us what to do next. Let's get out of here first and figure out the rest later!

choices.text: Paimon... quick... run... the power in this sword... it's overflowing...!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Eek! {NICKNAME}, what's happening— Hang on! Your acting is terrible! You can't start laughing halfway through your own prank! And quit scaring Paimon at a time like this!

talks.objective: Exit the Court of the First Edict

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, this must be the sword Aila was talking about, right?

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: Yes, yes! This is the sacred blade the first Moonchanter used to offer the very first drop of silver blood to the New Moon — a truly blessed sword of purity!

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: Ugh, I really want to investigate this place thoroughly... But if we hang around too long, Ehrnrooth, Uncle Krodo, and the others might find the entrance too...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Actually, with all the noise we made just now, there's probably no one on this whole island who hasn't been drawn this way...

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: Ugh, well... Since we've got the sword and the seal's already broken, I'll just have to find another time to study it properly!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh right, do you remember when Verna mentioned a place called the Court of the First Edict, when we were back at Thunderclap Reef?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon thinks it's somewhere over on Hiisi Island. If we've got some time to spare, why not go back and have a look?
